blocks.text: Quick verdict

Proxy-Cheap is the better choice for price-driven work on easier platforms: about $7.80 for 10 GB at its promotional rate against $45 at NodeMaven's pay-as-you-go rate, plus cheap static ISP and IPv6 IPs. NodeMaven is the better choice when a flagged IP costs you an account or an ad budget: its IP Quality Filter, long sticky sessions, quality guarantee and city and ISP targeting are built for social media and anti-detect browser work. Many operators use cheap IPs for warm-up tasks and NodeMaven for valuable accounts.

NodeMaven and Proxy-Cheap both sell residential, mobile and ISP proxies to multi-account operators and marketers, but at very different price points. Proxy-Cheap currently advertises rotating residential at $0.78/GB with no plan, and static ISP IPs for a few dollars a month. NodeMaven charges $2.20-$4.50/GB but filters every IP for fraud signals before assignment and pays out if proxies are bad. This comparison asks when clean IPs are worth roughly three to six times the price.

blocks.text: NodeMaven in 2026: what you get

NodeMaven is the quality-first option. Instead of handing out whatever IP the pool returns, it screens addresses in real time and lets you choose how strict the screening is. That matters most for account-based work such as social media management and multi-accounting, where a flagged IP can cost you an account. The price reflects it: $4.50/GB without a plan and $2.20/GB on monthly plans.

Strengths: IP Quality Filter screens IPs before you get them; Long sticky sessions for account work; Traffic rollover and cashback; Quality guarantee that pays for bad IPs. Weak spots: Smaller pool than mass-market networks; No datacenter proxies; Pay-as-you-go rate is double the plan rate.
Proxy-Cheap in 2026: what you get

Proxy-Cheap lives up to its name: rotating residential traffic is currently advertised at $0.78/GB (70% off a $2.60 list price) with no subscription, and static ISP and datacenter IPs cost a dollar or two per month. The catalog is broad, covering IPv6 options few competitors offer, and payment by card, PayPal, Alipay or crypto is easy. The trade-offs are thinner targeting (country and ISP rather than city on rotating residential) and less published performance data than the bigger brands.

Strengths: Very low per-GB price while the promotion runs; No monthly commitment on rotating residential; Broad catalog including IPv6 and static mobile; SOCKS5 with UDP support. Weak spots: Targeting is mostly country and ISP, not city; Residential pool size not separately published; Mixed results in some independent benchmarks.
Pricing: NodeMaven vs Proxy-Cheap

NodeMaven charges $4.50/GB pay-as-you-go and $2.20/GB on monthly plans, with residential and mobile traffic on one balance. A $3.50 trial includes 750 MB. Unused traffic rolls over, and you earn up to 10% cashback on used traffic. ISP proxies start at $2.99 per IP with unlimited traffic.

Proxy-Cheap's rotating residential proxies are pay-as-you-go, currently listed from $0.78/GB (a promotional price against a $2.60/GB list rate). Static residential ISP proxies start around $2.44 per IP per month, datacenter IPv4 at about $1.49, datacenter IPv6 from $0.15, and rotating mobile at $5.99/GB.

Buying 10 GB, you would pay about $7.80 with Proxy-Cheap and $45 with NodeMaven: a 83% saving in Proxy-Cheap's favour. At 100 GB a month, Proxy-Cheap is the cheaper option at about $78 against $220 for NodeMaven, roughly 65% less. The sticker price is only half of it. NodeMaven's unused traffic carries forward, while Proxy-Cheap's does not (pay-as-you-go balance, no monthly commitment), so if your usage swings from month to month NodeMaven can work out cheaper than the per-GB numbers suggest.
Pool size, coverage and targeting

Proxy-Cheap does not publish a clear residential pool figure, so a size comparison is not possible on published data. NodeMaven lists '30M+ residential + 250K mobile' and Proxy-Cheap lists 'Not separately published (155M+ claimed across all products)'. In practice, what matters is how many unique IPs you get in the countries you target, which you can measure in a short trial by sending a few thousand requests and counting distinct exit addresses. For coverage, NodeMaven lists 150+ countries and Proxy-Cheap lists 180+. On targeting, NodeMaven offers country, region, city and ISP, while Proxy-Cheap offers country and ISP.
Protocols, sessions and setup

Both providers support SOCKS5 as well as HTTP(S), so either will plug into scrapers, anti-detect browsers and automation tools that expect a SOCKS endpoint. On sessions, NodeMaven offers rotating or long sticky sessions (multi-day), and Proxy-Cheap offers rotating and sticky sessions. Setup works the same way on both: a single gateway endpoint, with location and session options passed as username parameters, plus IP whitelisting if you prefer not to use credentials.
Which is better for your use case?

General web scraping: close call. Both are reasonable choices here. NodeMaven: the quality filter matters less for high-rotation crawling. Proxy-Cheap: cheap traffic, though independent benchmark results have been mixed. Let price and the countries you need decide.

SERP and rank tracking: tie. Neither has a clear edge. With NodeMaven: workable, but you pay a premium for filtering you may not need. With Proxy-Cheap: workable for light rank tracking at a low cost. Run the same small test on both before committing.

Social media and multi-account management: NodeMaven. NodeMaven has the edge here. Why: pre-screened, low-fraud-score IPs with long sticky sessions. How Proxy-Cheap compares: cheap static ISP and mobile IPs for persistent identities.

E-commerce price and stock monitoring: tie. Neither has a clear edge. With NodeMaven: fine for light checks. With Proxy-Cheap: fine for country-level price checks. Run the same small test on both before committing.

Ad verification and geo-testing: NodeMaven wins. The deciding factor for NodeMaven: good quality but a smaller pool. The limitation on the Proxy-Cheap side: lacks city-level targeting on rotating residential.
Tight budgets: Proxy-Cheap wins. The deciding factor for Proxy-Cheap: the lowest advertised per-GB price in this pairing. The limitation on the NodeMaven side: mid-priced on plans, expensive on PAYG.
Trials, verification and billing fine print

Before you pay, check how each provider lets you test. NodeMaven: $3.50 trial with 750 MB. Proxy-Cheap: 7-day $1.99 trial on static residential and datacenter IPs. Verification and payment rules differ too. NodeMaven: Standard. Proxy-Cheap: Light; card, PayPal, Alipay and crypto accepted. Whichever you choose, measure cost per successful request rather than cost per gigabyte: retries, blocked pages and heavy page assets all burn bandwidth, and a cheaper network that fails more often can end up costing more. Blocking images and fonts in your scraper, reusing sessions where a target allows it, and capping concurrency are the quickest ways to cut the bill on either provider.
How to test NodeMaven and Proxy-Cheap before you commit
The quickest way to choose between NodeMaven and Proxy-Cheap is a side-by-side test on the sites and countries you actually care about:
1. Buy the smallest option on each side (NodeMaven: $3.50 trial with 750 MB; Proxy-Cheap: 7-day $1.99 trial on static residential and datacenter IPs).
2. Pick three to five real target URLs and the two or three countries that matter most, and send the same number of requests (a few hundred is enough) through each provider at the same time of day.

3. Record success rate, median response time, CAPTCHAs or blocks, and the number of unique exit IPs you received per country. 4. Divide what you spent by the number of successful, correctly located responses to get cost per useful request, then scale that to your monthly volume.
Bottom line

Across the six use cases above, NodeMaven comes out ahead in 2, Proxy-Cheap in 1, and 3 are ties. That makes NodeMaven the safer default if you are unsure, but the right answer still depends on your volume and targets: NodeMaven is strongest for social media and multi-account management, while Proxy-Cheap is strongest for price-sensitive scraping at moderate difficulty. If you can, spend a few dollars testing both on the exact sites and countries you care about; a one-hour test tells you more than any spec sheet.
